Now that it has been widely available for a couple days, what is your opinion on the Steam controller?
Really not a fan of the button placement on the controller
So far I'm liking it. It has allowed me to play some keyboard, and mouse games like Legend of Grimrock from my couch which is all I really wanted out of this controller.

Its an obvious gen 1.

  • There is no reason for both trackpads to be the same size. The left one should be smaller.
  • The left one should also double as a d-pad, inverting the impression so it feels right.
  • The top bumpers should be removed, the underside triggers are simply better and keeping 2 sets of fingers up top for bumpers and triggers is unwieldy.
  • It's too thick, massively too thick, especially at the bottom but its too thick top to bottom (and I have big hands).
  • Toss the thumb stick out, move the SSS buttons down there and shrink the size some left to right.
  • The ABXY buttons are too far center, you'll hit Y when trying to hit X... a lot.
  • The battery cover/grip trigger gives me anxiety, I doubt it'll last a year.
  • The gyro controls for fine tune aiming are a MASSIVE MASSIVE improvement compared to not enabling them. It's intuitive and should be defaulted.
  • Why the fuck is it not bluetooth? The proprietary dongle is a terrible idea. The range is fuck all too.

BUT

  • I am getting more and more accustomed to it.
  • Web browsing with it in windows is surprisingly good.
  • haptics once toned down are awesome
  • trackball mode is surprisingly good
  • it does more and it does it better than I was expecting and that makes it worth the purchase.
Maybe they could have just used an xbox one controller and replaced the dpad with a touch pad. You only need one touch pad to control games that require a mouse anyway.

I haven't used it all that much yet, but the one big improvement for me is having the track pads instead of analog sticks. I have rather small hands to begin with and an injury to my left thumb made using analog sticks particularly challenging. It's still a bit difficult to get it to work correctly with everything, but I think time and experimentation will improve that.

So for now, two thumbs up! (Pun intended.)

Edit: I'm not sure I could use for FPSes though. I haven't tried yet. I'm way too addicted to the ease of aiming with a mouse. I know trying to play such using the trackpad on my laptop is just about impossible.

By "the future", you mean rehashing something that was around 20 years ago? I had an NES controller that worked like this, and it wasn't as fun to use as the old square ones. I'm getting my steam controller in a week though, so I'll let you know how I feel about it now. Or maybe I won't.

I don't own one, but I did use the one my friend owns the other day.

It's fairly comfortable. I have pretty large hands, and it fits nicely in them.

The trackpad is...neat? It seemed to be a bit wonky, overly sensitive at times, and almost entirely unresponsive at others. That could have been some of the settings my friend was using though. I'd like to try it with Street Fighter 5, or something of that nature. I'm notoriously awful at fighting games, and perhaps the trackpad would be a bit more comfortable for me to use.

The L/R buttons on top are HUGE and unwieldy. I kept having to look to see which one I was hitting because this was my first time using the controller, and because they were so freaking big and close to each other.

The buttons on the back of the grip are a really cool idea, and I like them a lot, but they feel a bit odd. Probably because I'm used to the buttons on my Logitech Dual Action. I think they're in a good spot that feels natural, but the actuation on them is a bit iffy.

The ABXY buttons are off in the middle of nowhere, way to damned far away. Switch those and the right trackpad, and then make the trackpad a thumbstick.

The trackpads are also buttons, and my hand tended to slip on them a bit, or accidentally hit them.

My brief period of testing was on Batman: Arkham...something. I get the feeling that they were going for something like an updated N64/X-Box hybrid, and that they should have leaned a bit more on the N64 part.

It's a neat controller, but I don't think I'd drop $50 on it. That might be partially because I'm so used to this Logitech that is basically a Playstation controller, which is one of my favorite controllers ever. I think a rechargeable battery and charging cradle would be a fantastic addition.
